headline: COP31's CCUS and carbon-removal targets head into final-stretch negotiations amid EU resistance
summary: As COP31 nears its scheduled Friday close in Antalya, the draft cover decision's proposed first-ever CCUS goal (~500 Mt CO2/yr by 2035, 1.3-2.5 Gt/yr long-term) and broad CDR language remain contested, with the EU resisting and advocates warning against open-ended and marine CDR.
co2crc_note: First-ever COP-level CCUS capacity goal would set the global policy frame CO2CRC's Australian CCS work operates within.
extractor_note: 500 Mt is a draft policy target, not a commitment; capacity_mtpa is a policy-target figure, non-additive.

headline: UK carbon capture 'keeps advancing despite critics'
summary: An OilPrice commentary argues the UK's state-backed CCS programme keeps progressing despite criticism over cost, deliverability and capture plants' dependence on still-unbuilt transport-and-storage clusters.
co2crc_note: UK social-licence commentary; peripheral to CO2CRC but tracks the pro/anti-CCS public debate.

headline: UK Budget 2026 reportedly cuts ~GBP200m from carbon-capture capital grants
summary: Trade coverage says the latest UK Budget trimmed roughly GBP200m from CCS capital support, leaving Acorn and the Scottish Cluster without a confirmed commitment and clouding the FID outlook for the consented 910 MW Peterhead CCS power station.
co2crc_note: A major economy pulling back CCS grant support is a cautionary signal for public-funding-dependent CCS, including Australian programmes.
extractor_note: Date unverified (WebFetch blocked); amount and whether the Budget fell in-window both unconfirmed - radar only.

headline: COP31: carbon capture emerging as a strategic tool for exporters facing EU CBAM
summary: Carbon Herald side-event coverage frames CCS as a hedge for industrial exporters exposed to the EU carbon border adjustment mechanism.
co2crc_note: CBAM-driven demand for capture reshapes export economics relevant to Australian industrial emitters.

headline: Canada-Alberta-Pathways binding CCS agreements targeted for ~15 Nov
summary: The July trilateral MoU set a mid-November deadline for binding deals underpinning the C$16bn+ Pathways Alliance oil-sands CCS network; no confirmation of signing has surfaced.
co2crc_note: A marquee North American oil-sands CCS network; reference point for large-scale government-industry CCS deals.
extractor_note: Binding-agreement signing unconfirmed; capacity 6 Mtpa is the Phase-1 target, non-additive. Radar only.
